title:
U.S. Broadens Iran Pressure.
Poland Begins Mourning.
Japan Assesses a Quake.
subject: U.S. Broadens Iran Pressure. Poland Begins Mourning. Japan Assesses a Quake.
preview_text: A new U.S. task force, Poland’s investigation and Japan’s quake, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: The U.S. expands its Iran pressure campaign beyond sea routes, Poland begins mourning and Japan assesses earthquake damage.
contents_extra: Israel’s coalition arithmetic, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: A New U.S. Task Force Targets Iran’s Land and Caspian Trade Routes
paragraphs: The U.S. military is establishing Task Force Iron Gate to restrict advanced weapons and sanctioned materials crossing Iran’s land borders and the Caspian Sea. Reuters reports that the team will be based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other U.S. agencies, extending Washington’s pressure campaign beyond the existing naval blockade.

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards dismissed the effort Sunday, saying Tehran had prepared and maintained contact with neighboring countries. Reuters attributes that response to spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi. Reuters reports that the task force also targets dual use technology and revenue streams Washington calls illegal. The initiative follows months of naval restrictions on Iran.

stories.title: Poland’s Mourning Period Begins With Questions Across Two Crime Scenes
paragraphs: Mourners left candles in Krakow after Saturday’s shooting in the city’s Main Square. Six people were killed, and police detained the wounded suspected gunman. AP reports that Poland began two days of national mourning Sunday. Authorities also found three bodies at his family home in a separate city.

Officials are investigating possible influence from extreme nationalist ideology, alongside the suspect’s access to weapons. Reuters reports that national security agencies are helping police. The two officers who stopped the attacker remain hospitalized. Police said the 24 year old suspect had a firearms license and found weapons in his vehicle.

stories.title: Japan Warns of Aftershocks Following a Central Region Earthquake
paragraphs: Japan’s Meteorological Agency warned of possible strong aftershocks after an overnight earthquake centered in Shizuoka Prefecture. AP reports the agency measured a magnitude of 5.7. At least 22 people were reported injured in the AP account checked at 10:49 UTC. Some were hurt falling on stairs while fleeing buildings.

The quake struck at 1:04 a.m. Sunday, with the strongest shaking recorded in neighboring Aichi Prefecture. AP reports broken store windows and scattered books. The U.S. Geological Survey gave a magnitude of 5.5. Bullet trains slowed as a precaution, while the meteorological agency warned of possible mudslides and falling rocks.

deep_dive.title: Eisenkot Faces Coalition Talks Without an Assured Majority
paragraphs: President Isaac Herzog has selected Gadi Eisenkot to make the first attempt at forming Israel’s next government. AP reports that the opposition leader emerged from consultations with broad recommendations. But neither main bloc won a majority in the Oct. 27 election. Netanyahu’s Likud was the largest individual party, while his governing coalition lost its majority.

The arithmetic makes smaller parties important, but recommendations do not settle participation in a government. ABC reports that 67 lawmakers recommended Eisenkot during Herzog’s consultations. The former military chief must turn that support into an arrangement that can govern. His own bloc includes politicians who oppose relying on Arab led parties for parliamentary support.

Possible routes include an agreement with Arab led parties, outside support for a minority government, or a broader unity arrangement. Reuters reports deep obstacles to coalition building after the deadlocked vote. AP describes disagreements over military service exemptions and a formal investigation into the Oct. 7 security failures. None of these alternatives is an agreed coalition.

Eisenkot initially has 28 days to form a government, with a possible further 14 days. ABC reports that Herzog plans to make the formal offer Sunday. If the effort fails, Herzog could ask Netanyahu to try forming a government. A continuing deadlock could lead to fresh elections in the new year.

trivia.question: Where will the new Task Force Iron Gate be based?
trivia.explanation: A. Tampa, Florida. Reuters reports that the new U.S. military task force will be based there.

World view: Damascus denies troop plans for Yemen. A Syrian diplomatic source rejected deployment reports while leaving room for expanded Saudi military cooperation; Reuters reports.
Hong Kong’s legislature pushes back. Lawmakers condemned overseas criticism of an additional sentence imposed on democracy activist Joshua Wong; Reuters reports.
Malaysia’s royal decree faces scrutiny. The king warned against challenges to his order allowing Najib Razak’s transfer to house arrest; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Pollution changes Delhi routines. Schools were told to offer remote lessons before Diwali, while officials encouraged people to work from home; Reuters reports.
An arthritis pill shows trial gains. Johnson & Johnson reported better symptom improvement than placebo after 16 weeks in a late stage study; Reuters reports.
A heart treatment misses key outcomes. Novartis’ experimental drug lowered a blood marker but did not reduce major cardiovascular events in trial results; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Google takes over a Wyoming campus. Crusoe completed its predevelopment work; financial terms of the site acquisition were not disclosed; Reuters reports.
Egypt pursues Libyan energy connections. A minister described plans for gas links, oil refining and electricity projects, without detailing their costs; Reuters reports.
France’s Melenchon proposes stimulus. The presidential hopeful presented his economic program Saturday and renewed criticism of NATO; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: A double ring surrounds a dying star’s remnant. Researchers say the unusual white dwarf system may contain surviving planetary bodies; Reuters reports.
Turkish landfills reveal methane gaps. Satellites detected large releases even at sites with gas collection infrastructure; Reuters reports.
Kyiv describes a Russian satellite network. Ukraine’s military intelligence says Rassvet is already supporting Russian military communications; Reuters reports.
The score: Denver wins in Mexico City. The Nuggets beat Indiana 114 to 102, with Nikola Jokic adding 19 points; Reuters reports.
New York wins in Cleveland. The Knicks beat the Cavaliers 109 to 97 behind Jalen Brunson’s 31 points; Reuters reports.
Arsenal defeats Hull 1 to 0. Martin Odegaard scored the winner to extend Arsenal’s Premier League lead; The Guardian reports.
Life & culture: Nandy calls for industry accountability. The British minister said sexual abuse remains a problem in entertainment and women still fear speaking out; Reuters reports.
Everyday clothes inspire the Met’s next show. The announced exhibition will examine how designers transform ordinary materials and familiar garments; The Guardian reports.
Leo Sayer shares musical memories. In a new interview, the singer describes Bob Dylan’s influence and his memories of Bob Marley; The Guardian reports.

uncertainties: CNN reports White declined, citing a source; one aide called the offer a joke, and White publicly said he would meet Trump Monday.
Japan’s initial injury count and Poland’s investigation remain developing.
Task Force Iron Gate is a new initiative, not proof that trade routes have been closed.
Eisenkot has an opportunity to negotiate, not a confirmed coalition.
